summary: Retained with restrictions: station-day minor-flood exceedance. A (station, D) -> (station, D+1) join exposes the outcome day's observed_max_ft, giving near-perfect blind ranking (AUC ~0.9993, hundreds of binary mismatches against NOAA's official flag) in both split designs - not exact recovery, but far beyond honest modelling. The build and the data dictionary also disagree on the day definition (the build assigns the official minFlag to date+1).
supported_uses: Retrospective model-development experiments under the runner's isolated-rows interface: public eval rows for development and model selection, sealed labelled holdout for final scoring
Research use of the construction, provenance and honest baselines on the frozen artifact
unsupported_uses: Claims of verified real-time or operational forecasting validity
Unrestricted cross-row batch access to the public files as a benchmark surface
Reporting public-eval scores as out-of-sample forecasting skill
Any benchmark score produced by a solver holding the public files: the future-measurement join ranks near-perfectly
Presenting the label as NOAA's official same-day flag until the day definition is corrected and documented

cross_row_audit.scope: Both split designs (temporal, station-disjoint) tested; temporal 88,915/89,038 covered AUC 0.99929 with 423 binary mismatches; station-disjoint 29,889/29,930 AUC 0.99922 with 191; a D+2 margin_ft variant still ranks ~0.9993, so deleting the obvious column is not a fix

limitations: Near-perfect future-outcome ranking in both split designs (see cross_row_audit scope).
Dictionary/build day-definition conflict: release/noaa-tide-flooding/code/build.py assigns the official minFlag to date+1 while DATA_DICTIONARY.md describes the target-day value.
One calendar week straddles train/eval in each design (244 temporal, 82 station-disjoint eval rows).
Historical feature/label availability is assumed from current snapshots, not verified against release vintages.
The current scorer passes the complete feature frame; isolation is not mechanically enforced.
required_actions: Run predictions through the isolated-rows interface once implemented (issue #17); the current scorer passes the complete feature frame and does not mechanically enforce prediction-time isolation
Keep the labelled holdout outside evaluated workspaces and never load later rows when scoring earlier targets
Correct the day-definition documentation conflict (editorial overlay; frozen bytes untouched) and state the raw-max/official-flag distinction on the public page.
Versioned rebuild with outcome-day measurements purged from solver-visible rows in both designs; re-run the blind join battery before stronger claims.
